newsitem.title: USA: Rawlings says retailers cautious on baseball.
newsitem.headline: Rawlings says retailers cautious on baseball.

text.p: Rawlings Sporting Goods Co Inc said Tuesday that retailers remain cautious about order baseball related sporting goods, two years after the World Series was cancelled due to a work stoppage.
"While the fans' disaffection for baseball has begun to subside the retailers are approaching the 1997 selling season with caution," Carl Shields, chairman and chief executive officer said.

"As a result, we expect the trend toward later receipt of retailer orders and shipments closer to and during the selling season to continue," he said. "This may have the effect of shifting the seasonality and quarterly results of the company."

Earlier Tuesday, Rawlings reported a net loss of $798,000, or $0.10 a share in the fourth quarter ended August 31, compared to a loss of $2.2 million, or $0.28 a share a year ago. The fourth quarter is typically slow for the company, Rawlings said.

Net revenues in the quarter were $23.8 million, up from net revenues of $21.7 million in the same quarter a year ago. Higher net revenues for baseball-related products and apparel partially offset by lower basketball and football and international net revenues were primarily responsible for the increase. --Reuters Chicago newsdesk, 312-408-8787
